title: KV cache miss telemetry collection notes
content:
Purpose:
Collect, aggregate and analyze telemetry specifically targeted at KV-cache miss behavior across the serving stack (router -> frontend -> inference workers). This doc is a practical runbook + scripts index for reproducing, collecting, and triaging cache-miss-driven tail latency. Notes are intentionally informal — playbook for on-call and perf owners.

Background / motivation:
- Cache misses are a dominant factor for tail latency in some prompt-heavy workloads where prefix reuse is low.
- Naive profiling (cpu flamegraphs on a single process) misses cross-service correlation: a miss shows up as wait time in the worker but the root cause can be router reordering / bad batching / KV store contention.
- Goal: produce an actionable trace + per-layer flamegraph + heatmap that makes misses visible and actionable.

What we collect (telemetry primitives):
- trace_id (W3C or internal) and request_id: surface-through all services; must be present in logs and perf artifacts.
- event timestamps: router_enqueue, router_send, worker_receive, kvcache_lookup_start, kvcache_lookup_end, model_infer_start, model_infer_end, kvcache_warm_hit.
- micro-samples: perf samples (cpu, cycles), off-cpu stacks (perf record -g --clockid=clock_gettime), and eBPF histograms for schedule and io waits.
- KV store metrics: per-shard QPS, median and p95 lookup latency, memtable compaction events.
- Inference runtime counters: kv-cache hit ratio per-segment, kv-cache deserialization time, l2 cache serialization.

Instrumentation points and lightweight probes:
- router: attach a simple tracer header injector middleware (adds trace_id) and emit router_enqueue/send timestamps. A tiny sidecar script tracer_injector.py exists in /infra/tools (see linked artifacts).
- worker (inference process): add a small probing hook that toggles verbose kv-cache tracing via env REDWOOD_KVC_TRACE=1 to flush micro-timestamps to /tmp/kvc_trace/<trace_id>.json. This avoids log noise for perf runs.
- kernel/user-space correlation: use bpftrace snippet kvcache-miss.bt to capture syscall / page-fault activity around kvcache lookup spans.

Scripts and utilities (quick inventory):
- kv-miss-collector.sh: wrapper that coordinates starting agent collectors across router and workers, collects /tmp/kvc_trace/*.json and merges into combined timeline.
- kv-heatmap.py: consumes merged traces and produces per-segment heatmap (CSV) for hit-rate vs time-of-day or batch-size.
- flame-from-record.sh: transforms perf.data into merged flamegraph.svg (uses perf script + stackcollapse-perf.pl + flamegraph.pl).
- ebpf-wait-hist.sh: runs bcc/eBPF helper to produce on-cpu vs off-cpu histograms specifically for the kvcache lookup function symbol list.
- replay-runner/ (local): small harness to replay recorded requests with exact input ids to reproduce miss frequency.

Example quick-repro steps (on staging cluster):
1) pick a trace_id from SLO-alert or frontend logs that showed p99 spike.
2) kubectl exec into router pod and worker pod; enable REDWOOD_KVC_TRACE=1 and restart worker gracefully (there's a -hot-reload flag that preserves sockets).
3) run: ./kv-miss-collector.sh --trace-id <trace_id> --duration 120 --collect-perf --collect-ebpf. This will:
   - start perf record -F 999 -g on the worker process (PID discovered by name),
   - start bpftrace kvcache-miss.bt (if enabled),
   - wait the duration, and then scp artifacts locally.
4) ./flame-from-record.sh perf.data -> flame.svg and open.
5) cat merged-trace.json | ./kv-heatmap.py --out heatmap.csv and plot.

Interpretation quick-guide:
- If flamegraph shows heavy time in kv_deserialize or remote_lookup path, but heatmap shows 0.0x hit rate, likely cold cache or eviction-induced misses. Investigate cache TTL and shard placement.
- If off-cpu histograms spike during kvcache_lookup, consider contention on the backing store (i.e., syscall blocking or network IO).
- If CPU stacks pin to memcpy and protobuf::Parse, the cost is in serialization — consider switching to faster binary format/zero-copy.

CI integration suggestions (perf CI job):
- Add a kvcache-miss-smoke workflow in perf CI that runs a short warm-up + targeted miss-heavy workload (use replay-runner inputs) and captures: perf.data, offcpu hist, merged traces.
- Upload artifacts to perftools S3 with path prefix: perf-ci/<branch>/<commit>/kvcache-miss/<timestamp>/.
- A lightweight assertion: p99 end-to-end latency under configured threshold OR increase flagged by >20% relative regression should open a regression issue.
- Use artifact retention TTL 30 days for these perf CI runs, unless triage is opened.

Storage and dashboards:
- Store merged trace JSON and perf.data in S3 per above.
- Dashboard: kvcache-miss-workbench (Grafana) showing request traces, heatmap, p50/p95/p99 split by request size and batch size. Panels: KV hit rate (series), Miss QPS, Miss lookup p95, Worker CPU busy fraction.

Triage playbook (when alerted on tail latency):
1) sanity check: confirm trace_id exists and trace spans show router->worker timeline.
2) run kv-miss-collector for 60-120s against live traces; prefer staging replica if traffic sensitive.
3) produce flamegraph + heatmap and check three buckets: serialization cost, remote lookup cost, and scheduling/wait.
4) correlate with infra metrics: disk IO, network, NFS (if backing store), GPU queue length.
5) if reproducible locally with replay-runner, iterate on micro-optimizations (serialization, pinning threads, pre-warm).
6) if systemic across many trace_ids, escalate to platform + storage team (tag with ENG-4128).

Common pitfalls / notes to self:
- perf record sampling frequency > 1000Hz on busy systems can skew timings; use 400-800Hz for reliable stacks.
- Flamegraphs without frame-ids are misleading when JIT/inlined code; confirm symbolization with addr2line in CI packaging.
- eBPF scripts require elevated privileges; for CI use a container image with CAP_SYS_ADMIN turned on, and keep scripts gating via env flag.
- Avoid long-running perf records on production; prefer short windows and multiple samples.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we standardize on a single on-disk trace format (protobuf vs JSON)? Right now merged-trace.json is ad-hoc.
- Build a small UX in console to request kvcache-miss capture and auto-attach artifacts to the trace in the console.
- Add automated parsing that maps flame hotspots to GitHub file + line for faster triage.

Appendix: quick commands
- Start perf on worker PID 1234: sudo perf record -F 800 -p 1234 -g -- sleep 60
- Generate flamegraph: sudo perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded; ./flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg
- Run bpftrace snippet: sudo bpftrace kvcache-miss.bt -c 'sleep 60'
- Merge traces (local): ./kv-miss-collector.sh --merge-only --src /tmp/kvc_trace/ --out merged-trace.json

Contact: Maya Patel (mayap@redwood.ai) — ping in #perf-ops on Slack for quick follow-ups.

End of notes.
